final_messages.text:
The PDF adds source-specific context, but it does not resolve the polygon conflict. Its legend distinguishes sub-prefecture, international, and undetermined boundaries; the map depicts Zémio on the CAR side. Its coarse, non-georeferenced map cannot establish that its boundary matches the pinned geoBoundaries feature or locate the 36 centers relative to that line.

I found no further specific accessible primary-source step in the retained evidence that would decide the exact feature-to-key relation. A proposal-only researched-unresolved disposition for these 36 is supportable if it records this limitation. Keep all 36 held; the map does not clear them.

The UNHCR record does not establish that the Zémio feature is inapplicable to the 36 Ango keys. Its humanitarian map and non-endorsement disclaimer limit claims about legal authority, but the exact center hits remain adverse evidence. The pinned feature’s identity with the PDF geometry is also unverified.

One reasonable step remains: inspect the actual PDF and its map legend through the ordinary document URL with a PDF-capable reader. This may clarify the map’s geographic context, though it may not decide exact applicability. Keep the 36 keys held and the conflict unresolved. Preserve the differing license records as stated; do not infer one license from the other.

The 36-key join confirms a specific conflict: every center falls inside both COD Ango and CAF ADM2 Zémio; 28 also fall inside CAF ADM1 Haut-Mbomou. None hits the five CAF ADM3 or two SSD features. The exact source-evidence operands are represented, with no additional candidate family hits.

This does not clear the CAF exclusion. The original full-scope diagnostic need not be rerun, and a full-cell test would not resolve source applicability by itself. The evidence supports a narrowly scoped researched-unresolved proposal for these 36, provided it describes the Ango/Zémio overlap as unresolved and retains all 36 holds. It does not support qualification, repair, or credit.

The 14 pinned exclusions identify the retained CAF and SSD candidate features and their differing source vintages. That establishes the candidate set and provenance, but does not decide whether those features apply to individual Ango keys or clear the original exclusion evidence.

The existing full-scope diagnostic need not be rerun. The remaining step is a key-specific applicability review of any CAF/SSD contacts against the original qualification predicate. Keep all 36 held; the lineage pins alone do not support clearance or a researched-unresolved disposition.
